title: On Shaking the tree till the fruit fell
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：shake　|　正文 350 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 shake 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1986 the guide ① shook the tree till the fruit fell before dawn, and every traveller in the valley said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the guide ② shakes the tree till the fruit fell in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ shake the tree till the fruit fell at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ shaken the tree till the fruit fell before — a line in the guidebook for July 1980 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Shaking the tree till the fruit fell before dawn, the guide said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the map at the far ledge, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ shake hands with the oldest guest in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Shake hands with the oldest guest at once and never mention it again.

By 1993 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the guidebook, and a new traveller from the next valley ⑧ shakes hands with the oldest guest before dawn every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the ledge, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ shook the tree till the fruit fell again when nobody else would.

⑩ To shake the tree till the fruit fell, my mother said in 1998, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the valley remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the valley forgets, somebody shakes the tree till the fruit fell in public again and somebody must shake the tree till the fruit fell before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 摇（一般过去式 shook the tree till the fruit fell：1986 年向导头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 摇（一般现在 shakes the tree till the fruit fell：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 摇（不定式 to shake the tree till the fruit fell：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 摇（过去完成时 had shaken the tree till the fruit fell：1980 年七月的旅行手册上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 摇（动名词 shaking the tree till the fruit fell 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 握手（shake hands with the oldest guest：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去握手与最年长的客人握了手）
G. v. 握手（shake hands with the oldest guest：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 摇（后段两处：新来的旅人照例 shakes hands with the oldest guest，而母亲又一次 shook the tree till the fruit fell）

answers.why: shake 意为“摇”，1986 年向导天没亮就摇把树摇到果子落下来，那是山谷里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 shook。
shake 意为“摇”，自那以后向导当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 shakes。
shake 意为“摇”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯摇把树摇到果子落下来”，此处为不定式 to shake the tree till the fruit fell。
shake 意为“摇”，旅行手册里 七月 那行字说明早在 1993 年之前就有人摇过，故用过去完成时 had shaken。
shake 意为“摇”，向导说“摇把树摇到果子落下来这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 shaking the tree till the fruit fell 作主语。
shake 意为“握手”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去握手与最年长的客人握了手”，should ever 之后用原形 shake hands with the oldest guest。
shake 意为“握手”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻握手与最年长的客人握了手（shake hands with the oldest guest at once），以后再也不要提起。
shake 意为“摇”，新来的旅人每个日子都照例握手与最年长的客人握了手，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 shakes。
shake 意为“摇”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就摇把树摇到果子落下来，用一般过去式 shook 叙述。
shake 意为“摇”，结尾那句是母亲 1998 年的话：要摇把树摇到果子落下来，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和山谷记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 shake 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1986 the guide shook the tree till the fruit fell before dawn, and nobody in the valley forgot it.
Even now the guide shakes the tree till the fruit fell in public whenever the valley asks.
Shaking the tree till the fruit fell before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever shake hands with the oldest guest in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new traveller from the next valley shakes hands with the oldest guest before dawn every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother shook the tree till the fruit fell again, and the valley remembered that half.
